requirement: Wait for a page element with an explicit wait that polls a condition, ignores missing elements and times out, like Selenium's WebDriverWait.
skeleton: WaitTimeoutError and NoSuchElementError, a Wait class with an injectable clock and an until method, and two expected-condition factories.
caption: An explicit-wait helper modeled on Selenium's WebDriverWait, written in the standard library with time, typing Protocol and collections.abc and no third-party imports. Wait raises ValueError for a non-positive timeout or poll, and until evaluates the condition, returns the first truthy value, ignores NoSuchElementError, checks the deadline after each attempt with a strict comparison and raises WaitTimeoutError with the message. visibility_of_element_located and text_to_be_present build conditions over a duck-typed driver. The fixture asserts the polling schedule, the attempt count at timeout, falsy values keep polling, the text condition, and error propagation.

plan.intent: Wait for a button to appear
constraints: A non-positive timeout or poll raises ValueError
NoSuchElementError is ignored while polling, other exceptions propagate
Only truthy condition values end the wait
The deadline is checked after each attempt and exceeding it raises WaitTimeoutError
Visibility requires is_displayed to be true

rationale.teaches: Evaluate first, return on truthiness, swallow only the missing-element error and compare against the deadline strictly after each try.
rationale.why: Explicit waits fail subtly when they return hidden elements, treat empty values as success or give up one poll early.

ops.docstring: Poll a condition against a driver the way Selenium's WebDriverWait does.

ops.source:
class WaitTimeoutError(Exception):
    """Raised when the condition never became truthy before the deadline."""

class NoSuchElementError(Exception):
    """Raised by a driver when a locator matches nothing."""

candidates.why_wrong: The wait gives up one poll early when the clock lands exactly on the deadline.
A missing element aborts the wait instead of being retried.
A present but hidden element is returned as if it were visible.
An empty string or zero ends the wait because only None is treated as pending.
A zero timeout or zero poll interval is accepted instead of raising ValueError.
